newsitem.title: USA: Icelandair to start Minneapolis service in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Icelandair to start Minneapolis service in 1998.

text.p: Icelandair will begin offering service from Minneapolis/St. Paul, Minnesota, to Iceland with connections to 20 European cities in April 1998, the Metropolitan Airports Commission said Saturday.
The airline will offer non-stop flights to Iceland four times a week. Final destinations include Britain, Scandinavia and other continental European sites.

Northwest Airlines Corp, with its partner KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV, also offers transatlantic service from the airport. Northwest, based at the Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport, will provide ground-handling services for Icelandair.
The Metropolitan Airports Commission is an independent agency which owns and operates the airport.
